selection.runtime: existing software AES and original small buffers
selection.summary: Keep the existing software AES runtime. Neither larger-buffer prototype establishes a useful hosted gain. The native path increases published-job CPU. The larger software batches also show no CPU reduction. Both runtime prototypes are removed; their exact sources remain archived. New public benchmark correlation and the corrected activation fixtures remain.
selection.limits: The final software client has a driver interruption. Its complete throughput remains unqualified. Runtime variation and different rejection counts prevent a causal end-to-end speed estimate.

limits: Private Router measurements exclude browser transport and public Gateway approval.
Successful HTTP latency excludes preceding admission waits.
Qualified means capture/version/accounting qualification, not universal request success.
Positive completion receipts do not prove all durable publication outcomes.
Retired state does not distinguish a physical burn from unlogged consumption.
No hosted speedup is established by either prototype.

complete_cycle.scope: Finite load plus the earliest captured set of full reserve observations, each no older than 45 seconds. Observation delay is included. This is not a maximum-capacity claim.

authority_version_coverage.scope: Unfiltered admission actor invocation versions during the load window. The public Router version alone does not establish the effective policy.

complete_cycle_ledger.retirement_limit: Retired proves unavailability, not burn versus unlogged consumption.
